draft.title: Deep Time and continuous cultures
card: Deep Time means the very long span of time before written records, when people were already living in Australia. For Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, it covers tens of thousands of years.
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have lived in Australia for that whole span. They are the First Peoples of this continent.
A continuous culture is one that has been passed on from generation to generation without a break. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures are the world's oldest continuous cultures.
Many cultures around the world are very old. What sets these cultures apart is the length of time they have carried on, while also changing and adapting.
draft.remember: Deep Time is tens of thousands of years, and these are the world's oldest continuous cultures.

a.q: What does it mean to call a culture continuous?
opts: It has been passed on through generations without a break
It has stayed exactly the same since it began
It has been written down in books from the start
It began when other cultures first made contact
a.why: Continuous means the culture has been handed on from one generation to the next without a break. It does not mean it never changed, because the card says these cultures have also adapted.
a.clue: Think about passing something on from parents to children.

b.q: Priya says Deep Time began when Europeans first wrote about Australia. Why is she wrong?
opts: People were living here for tens of thousands of years before
Deep Time only covers the time of the dinosaurs
Deep Time covers only the last few hundred years
Deep Time describes the time before any people lived here
b.why: Deep Time is the very long span of time before written records, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples were living in Australia throughout it. Starting it at European writing wrongly ignores tens of thousands of years of human life.
b.clue: Were people living here before anyone wrote records?
